arxiv-1904-06465.title: Differential extinction of Vibrational Molecular Overtone Transitions with Gold Nanorods and Non-Trivial Surface Enhanced Near-IR Absorption (SENIRA)
arxiv-1904-06465.creator: Daler R. Dadadzhanov, Tigran A. Vartanyan, Alina Karabchevsky
arxiv-1904-06465.description: Abstract Resonant coupling between plasmonic nanoantennas and molecular vibrational excitations is employed to amplify the weak overtone transitions that reside in the near-infrared. We explore for the first time the differential extinction of forbidden molecular overtone transitions coupled to the localized surface plasmons.

arxiv-2107-01390.creator: Doctor of Philosophy
arxiv-2107-01390.description: Abstract Memory and attention in deep learning by Hung Thai Le BSc. (Honours) Deakin University August 2019 Abstract Intelligence necessitates memory. Without memory, humans fail to perform various nontrivial tasks such as reading novels, playing games or solving maths .

arxiv-2110-00977.title: Class of quasiprobability distributions of work and initial quantum coherence
arxiv-2110-00977.creator: Gianluca Francica
arxiv-2110-00977.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gianluca Francica. The work is a concept of fundamental importance in thermodynamics. An open question is how to describe the work fluctuation for quantum coherent processes in the presence of initial quantum coherence in the energy basis. With the aim of giving a unified description, here we introduce and study a class of quasiprobability distributions of work, which give an average work equal to the average energy change of the system and reduce to the two-projective measurement scheme for an initial incoherent state.

arxiv-2204-01826.title: Revealing Cumulative Risks in Online Personal Information: A Data Narrative Study Conference: CSCW ’22:THE 25TH ACM CONFERENCE ON COMPUTER-SUPPORTED COOPERATIVE WORK AND SOCIAL COMPUTING; Nov 12–16, 2022; Taipei CCS: Human-centered computing → Human computer interaction (HCI); Empirical studies in H
arxiv-2204-01826.creator: Emma Nicol, Jo Briggs, Wendy Moncur, Amal Htait, Daniel Carey, Leif Azzopardi, Burkhard Schafer
arxiv-2204-01826.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emma Nicol, Jo Briggs, Wendy Moncur, Amal Htait, Daniel Carey, Leif Azzopardi, Burkhard Schafer. When pieces from an individual’s personal information available online are connected over time and across multiple platforms, this more complete digital trace can give unintended insights into their life and opinions. In a data narrative interview study with 26 currently employed participants, we examined risks and harms to individuals and employers when others joined the dots between their online information.

arxiv-2206-01073.title: The contact process on dynamical scale-free networks
arxiv-2206-01073.creator: Emmanuel Jacob, Amitai Linker and Peter Mörters
arxiv-2206-01073.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emmanuel Jacob, Amitai Linker and Peter Mörters. Abstract: We investigate the contact process on four different types of scale-free inhomogeneous random graphs evolving according to a stationary dynamics, where each potential edge is updated with a rate depending on the strength of the adjacent vertices.

arxiv-2304-00891.title: Online Algorithms for Hierarchical Inference in Deep Learning applications at the Edge
arxiv-2304-00891.creator: Vishnu Narayanan Moothedath 1 {}^{\textbf{1}}, \IEEEmembership Jaya Prakash Champati 2 {}^{\textbf{2}}, \IEEEmembership and James Gross 3 {}^{\textbf{3}} \IEEEmembership
arxiv-2304-00891.description: Abstract We consider a resource-constrained Edge Device (ED), such as an IoT sensor or a microcontroller unit, embedded with a small-size ML model (S-ML) for a generic classification application and an Edge Server (ES) that hosts a large-size ML model (L-ML).

arxiv-2312-14745.title: Strengthening Nash Equilibria
arxiv-2312-14745.creator: Ivan Geffner, Moshe Tennenholtz
arxiv-2312-14745.description: Abstract Nash equilibrium is often heralded as a guiding principle for rational decision-making in strategic interactions. However, it is well-known that Nash equilibrium sometimes fails as a reliable predictor of outcomes, with two of the most notable issues being the fact that it is not resilient to collusion and that there may be multiple Nash equilibria in a single game.

arxiv-2503-12970.title: Entropic bottlenecks to nematic ordering in an R ​ P 2 RP^{2} apolar spin model
arxiv-2503-12970.creator: B. Kamala Latha 1, V.S.S. Sastry 2, S. R. Shenoy 3
arxiv-2503-12970.description: Abstract The Lebwohl-Lasher model of uniaxial liquid crystals with ( n = 3, d = 2) was reported earlier to undergo a crossover transition to a novel nematic phase at a temperature T = T n T=T_{n} . This phase has unbound topological defects in a nematic background, that pair at a lower T BKT < T n T_{\text{BKT}}<T_{n} .

arxiv-2511-17969.title: Density functional theory for core-level X-ray absorption
arxiv-2511-17969.creator: Seokkyu An, Taisuke Ozaki
arxiv-2511-17969.description: Abstract We establish a rigorous density functional theory (DFT) framework for core-level X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) by formulating a constrained search for core-excited states based on the Gunnarsson-Lundqvist theorem. Within this framework, the explicit-core Δ \Delta SCF scheme enables shift-free absolute edge alignment and a consistent treatment of L/M edges with spin-orbit-resolved projectors.

arxiv-2601-03968.title: The uniqueness and concentration behavior of solutions for a nonlinear fractional Schrödinger system
arxiv-2601-03968.creator: Chungen Liu, Zhigao Zhang, Jiabin Zuo
arxiv-2601-03968.description: Abstract Abstract. The paper is concerned with a nonlinear system of two coupled fractional Schrödinger equations with both attractive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions in \mathbb{R} . By analyzing an associated L^{2} -constrained minimization problem, the uniqueness of solutions to this system is proved via the implicit function theorem.

plos-pone-0007127.description: PLOS ONE research article. However, these t

pmc-10508613.title: On the interpretation of transcriptome-wide association studies
pmc-10508613.creator: Christiaan de Leeuw, Josefin Werme, Jeanne E. Savage, Wouter J. Peyrot, Danielle Posthuma
pmc-10508613.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) aim to detect relationships between gene expression and a phenotype, and are commonly used for secondary analysis of genome-wide association study (GWAS) results. Results from TWAS analyses are often interpreted as indicating a genetic relationship between gene expression and a phenotype, but this interpretation is not consistent with the null hypothesis that is evaluated in the traditional TWAS framework.

pmc-11473954.title: Adaptive segmentation-to-survival learning for survival prediction from multi-modality medical images
pmc-11473954.creator: Mingyuan Meng, Bingxin Gu, Michael Fulham, Shaoli Song, Dagan Feng, Lei Bi, Jinman Kim
pmc-11473954.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Early survival prediction is vital for the clinical management of cancer patients, as tumors can be better controlled with personalized treatment planning. Traditional survival prediction methods are based on radiomics feature engineering and/or clinical indicators (e.g., cancer staging). Recently, survival prediction models with advances in deep learning techniques have achieved state-of-the-art performance in end-to-end survival prediction by exploiting deep features derived from medical images.

pmc-11574062.title: Hemoadsorption improves kidney microcirculatory oxygenation and oxygen consumption, ameliorates tubular injury, and improves kidney function in a rat model of sepsis-induced AKI
pmc-11574062.creator: Bülent Ergin, Deniz Erol Kutucu, Aysegul Kapucu, Wijnie van Dam, Lorenza Moretto, Paul Heyman, Can Ince
pmc-11574062.description: Microcirculatory dysfunction, hypoxia, and inflammation are considered to be central in the pathogenesis of sepsis-induced acute kidney injury (AKI). In this experimental study, we hypothesized that extracorporeal removal of inflammatory cytokines by hemoadsorption (HA) therapy may mitigate renal injury associated with sepsis-induced AKI.

pmc-11862376.title: Exploring Exercise Intervention as a Therapeutic Catalyst within the Mental Health and Addiction Program in Nova Scotia: A Proof-of-Concept Study
pmc-11862376.creator: S Obeng Nkrumah, R da Luz Dias, E Eboreime, B Agyapong, S Sridharan, V I O Agyapong
pmc-11862376.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionMany mental health conditions, including anxiety, mood disorders, and depression, can be effectively treated at a relatively low cost. Exercise interventions can be a therapeutic strategy, but even though exercise has consistently been shown to improve physical health, cognitive function, and psychological well-being, as well as reduce depression and anxiety symptoms, this intervention is often neglected in mental health care services.ObjectivesThe study aims to assess the feasibility of incorporating an Exercise Intervention Program (EIP) as a therapeutic pathway within the Mental Health

pmc-12374360.title: Nanoengineered hydrogels disrupt tumor antioxidant defense via photothermal-chemodynamic synergy and oxidative stress boosts
pmc-12374360.creator: Leiguang Ye, Yang Qiao, Peisan Wang, Wei Li, Xianwen Wang, Yiqun Zhang, Zhennan Yuan
pmc-12374360.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). By integrating photothermal and chemodynamic properties, Ru-based nanomaterials have emerged as promising agents for tumor therapy. However, their clinical translation is hindered by high systemic toxicity, suboptimal therapeutic efficacy, and compromised chemodynamic performance caused by tumor antioxidant defense mechanisms. A multifunctional therapeutic platform (Ru-PC-PEITC-ALG) was developed through the coordination-driven self-assembly of ruthenium ions with procyanidins (PCs) to form Ru-PC nanoparticles, followed by coencapsulation with phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC) in a sodium alginate hydrogel.

pmc-12520778.title: Application of remote sensing and geospatial technologies in predicting vector-borne disease outbreaks
pmc-12520778.creator: Ebrahim Abbasi
pmc-12520778.description: Vector-borne diseases (VBDs) pose significant global health threats, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Remote sensing (RS) and geospatial technologies offer valuable tools for monitoring environmental changes and predicting disease transmission patterns, thereby supporting proactive public health interventions. This study reviews the application of RS and geospatial methods in the prediction, monitoring and control of VBDs.

pmc-12609521.title: Deep Learning Network with Illuminant Augmentation for Diabetic Retinopathy Segmentation Using Comprehensive Anatomical Context Integration
pmc-12609521.creator: Sakon Chankhachon, Supaporn Kansomkeat, Patama Bhurayanontachai, Sathit Intajag, Jae-Ho Han
pmc-12609521.description: Background/Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) segmentation faces critical challenges from domain shift and false positives caused by heterogeneous retinal backgrounds. Recent transformer-based studies have shown that existing approaches do not comprehensively integrate the anatomical context, particularly training datasets combining blood vessels with DR lesions.

pmc-13111612.title: Chromosomal-level genome assembly of Ichthyurus bourgeoisi Gestro using PacBio HiFi and Hi-C sequencing
pmc-13111612.creator: Yuxia Yang, Yiyang Zhen, Zheng Yang, Jiliang Wang, Jianxin Hua, Haoyu Liu
pmc-13111612.description: Ichthyurus bourgeoisi Gestro is a representative species of the tribe Ichthyurini within the beetle family Cantharidae. This tribe is particularly noteworthy because of its brachelytrous characteristics. However, the lack of high-quality genomic resources hinders our understanding of the evolution and ecological adaptions associated with this beetle group. In this study, we present a chromosome-level genome assembly for I.

pmc-13148467.title: Customizable FDM-based zebrafish larva mold for live imaging
pmc-13148467.creator: Marcela Xiomara Rivera Pineda, Jaakko Lehtimäki, Guillaume Jacquemet
pmc-13148467.description: Accurate and reproducible orientation of zebrafish larvae is essential for high-resolution live imaging but remains difficult with standard agarose mounting. Although previous methods have used 3D-printed tools, often fabricated via stereolithography, here, we present an orientation tool made via fused deposition modeling and enhanced with a thin resin coating to improve surface smoothness and performance.

pmc-13204066.title: Surgical Management of Traumatic Brain Injury Based on Intracranial Compliance: Toward Personalized Decision-Making
pmc-13204066.creator: Santiago Cardona-Collazos, Laura M. Loaiza-Cardona, Andres Salazar-Restrepo, Luigi Valentino Berra, Andres M. Rubiano
pmc-13204066.description: Highlights What are the main findings? •The framework of surgical management of the intracranial compartment syndrome shifts surgical reasoning from lesion-centered thresholds to physiology-centered management.•What ultimately drives the neurosurgical intervention are not numerical values, but the loss of intracranial compliance and the physiological consequences that follow. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13356992.title: Bridging the attitude–behaviour gap in blood donation: A large‐scale knowledge–attitudes–practices study among university students in China
pmc-13356992.creator: Li Zhao, Jianhuai Jin, Jiali Yao, Ling Chen
pmc-13356992.description: Background and ObjectivesUniversity students are a vital yet underutilized donor population, constrained by a knowledge–attitude–practice (KAP) gap. We sought to assess the KAP status and identify modifiable determinants of blood donation among university students in a major Chinese city to inform targeted recruitment strategies.
